newsitem.title: UK: Spanish EMU expectations off highs - JP Morgan index.
newsitem.headline: Spanish EMU expectations off highs - JP Morgan index.

text.p: Market expectations of a broad-based European monetary union stayed buoyant over the past week but the probability of Spain taking part has been scaled back from heady highs, according to JP Morgan's EMU calculator.

In the past five trading days, market prices indicate that the perceived probability Spain joining EMU in 1999 retreated four percentage points to 82 percent. The probability of Sweden, Italy, Denmark and the UK taking part all edged higher.

The retreat in Spain came in the face of a strong peseta rally last week, traders said. Nevertheless, probabilities in Spain, Sweden and Italy are all still above 70 percent and Spain remains the highest.
According to these calculations, the market still believes there is a 100 percent chance France and Belgium will be in EMU in 1999, unchanged from last week.

JP Morgan's EMU calculator derives from the interest rate swaps market probabilities of individual countries joining Germany in EMU in 1999. The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
